inputs.obligation_targeted: SAL-XLIFF-OBL-7DA078717EA60881 and SAL-XLIFF-OBL-867500AA0AC3D2C1 (both XLIFF-MODEL-001) -- remain partial, evidence strengthened with a genuinely new, narrow capability
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 5 new tests prove: a locally declared value always wins over the parent; an absent value inherits the parent's effective value; <data> always defaults to preserve regardless of parent; an explicit value on <data> still wins over its own fixed default; the function's own default parent argument matches the root's spec-mandated default.

execution_steps: 1. Re-read both obligations' missing_behavior text: 'nothing walks up the tree to resolve an effective xml:space/xml:lang (or any other inheritable attribute) for a descendant that does not declare it locally.' Deliberately scoped this tick to xml:space only, the obligation's own concrete named example, not xml:lang or a fully generic 'any inheritable attribute' framework.

2. Re-confirmed the pinned XLIFF 2.1 spec's own default-value table for xml:space (section 4.3.2.2, already extracted earlier this session): 'default values for this attribute depend on the element in which it is used: When used in <data>: The value preserve. When used in <xliff>: The value default. When used in any other element: The value of the xml:space attribute of its parent element.' A complete, unambiguous, 3-branch rule with no remaining ambiguity.

3. Deliberately chose to build the resolution RULE as a reusable primitive function (effective_xml_space(local_value, *, parent, is_data)) rather than a full tree-walking API: this package's model has no parent back-references anywhere (confirmed by the prior grep this obligation's own evidence already cites), so a true 'ask any node its own effective value' method would require either adding parent pointers or redesigning the tree -- a genuine, larger architecture decision correctly deferred without dedicated design review, matching this session's established discipline for similarly-shaped questions (UBL-WRITE-001's auto-reordering, XLIFF's own tolerant-recovery-mode obligation, both left deliberately unbuilt for the same reason).

4. Added effective_xml_space() to model/document.py, next to the existing XliffDocument.xml_space property it complements (that property answers the root case; this function answers every other element, including <data>'s own distinct fixed default).
5. Exported the new function from model/__init__.py and the package's own top-level __init__.py, following the exact same export pattern already used for every other public model function.

6. Probed directly before writing formal tests: local value always wins regardless of parent or is_data; absent value inherits parent for both 'default' and 'preserve' parents; is_data=True always returns 'preserve' regardless of parent, even when the caller passes a non-default parent; an explicit local value on data still overrides its own fixed default. All 6 probes correct on the first attempt.

7. Wrote 5 formal tests in a new file (test_obligation_xml_space_inheritance_resolution.py, a fresh capability angle distinct from the existing root-only xml_space test file), all passing on the first attempt.

8. Ran ruff (clean), the full xliff suite (466 passed, was 461, +5), and the full 6-format regression (3421 passed, was 3416, +5; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.

9. Ran skills-first governance: resolve -> add-python-api (COMPOSE_EXISTING_SKILLS), manifest create --write (sfx-6be6fd11461bddd0, confirmed as the actually-persisted manifest via ls -t .local/skills-first/manifests/), hand-written receipt YAML, closeout --close -> CLOSE_OK.

10. Kept both obligations at partial, not promoted to implemented: this slice proves the xml:space resolution RULE completely and honestly, but composing it across an actual document tree (the caller-facing 'give me this unit's effective xml:space' experience the obligation's own rule_text implies) remains unbuilt, as does xml:lang's separate inheritance chain entirely. Updated missing_behavior to precisely reflect this narrower remaining scope rather than leaving the old, now partially-stale 'nothing exists at all' framing.
